Subject: Service availability framework — initial ask

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — OptiHealth is excited to move the pilot into production next quarter. Procurement asked me to capture the SLA expectations up front so we can map internal approvals. Key asks from our side:

- Baseline uptime for hosted inference during pilot (we need a firm percentage).
- Monthly monetary credit formulation if SLOs are missed (simple formula preferred).
- Latency SLOs for P95 inference latency (the digital triage flow is latency sensitive).
- Maintenance windows / blackout periods (we have peak hours 8am–6pm ET, Mon–Fri).
- Exceptions for batched offline jobs vs. real-time endpoints.

I attached an RFI with our preferred language (SLA_RFI_OptiHealth.pdf). We'd like a first-pass position from Redwood by EOD next week so procurement can include it in the vendor pack.

Also — any quick signal on caps for monthly credits? Procurement is nervous about open-ended exposure.

Thanks Daniel — great to work with you. Short answer up front so your procurement team can start slotting approvals:

- Hosted baseline uptime we typically offer for pilots: 99.95% (monthly). For production reserved/dedicated plans we can discuss 99.99% depending on commitment.
- Standard monthly credit: pro rata percentage of monthly invoice tied to severity bands; as a starter we propose up to 10% of the monthly invoice for a single-month breach, escalated bands for larger degradations.
- Latency: for single-turn real-time endpoints we can commit to P95 <= 300ms for typical short-form generation payloads under the pilot traffic profile.
- Maintenance: we propose a weekly scheduled maintenance window (1–2 hours off-peak) and a monthly maintenance allowance (up to 4 hours) — we can exempt scheduled maintenance with advance notice from credits.
- Exceptions: batched offline jobs should be carved out in the SLA and measured separately.

I'm looping Laura for legal redlines and Karthik to help size the traffic distribution and carveouts for batching. Attached is a first-pass doc (draft-sla-template-v1.docx) that maps the above into contract language — treat as discussion draft.

Would you and procurement be available for a 30-minute call on Tue 14 Sep to run through the credit cap and peak blackout periods? I'll include a HubSpot note with the deal id so everyone can comment.

Best,

Hi Daniel, Ben — looping in legal position and a couple of proposed guardrails. Thanks for the clear asks. Below are redline-level bullets from our side; I'll follow up with a marked-up document (redlines_sla.docx) by EOD.

Key proposed changes (legal):
1) Measurement window: uptime calculated monthly using provider-side metrics; remediation credits calculated as percentage of monthly invoice for the billing period in which the breach occurred.
2) Scheduled maintenance carveout: scheduled maintenance ( <= 4 hours per calendar month) is excluded from uptime calculation if customers receive >= 48 hours advance notice. We will offer one shorter emergency maintenance allowance with notice where practicable.
3) Credit cap: to address procurement concern, propose a per-month cap at 50% of the monthly invoice for material degradations. For pilots we are willing to lower the cap to 25% as a commercial concession (pilot cap).
4) Latency obligations: we can commit to P95 <= 300ms for synchronous endpoints under the documented traffic profile. We will not apply credits for transient latency spikes caused by customer traffic patterns outside of the agreed profile.
5) Batching carveout: batched, throughput-optimized jobs (e.g., offline bulk embeddings) will be excluded from the standard real-time uptime calculation and governed by a separate SLO with a different measurement cadence.
6) Escalation and remedies: incident response SLA (ack within 1 hour, engage for high-severity within 4 hours) and a runbook-triggered root cause timeline; extended remediation/rescheduling language to avoid open-ended liability.

Please confirm whether OptiHealth can accept the pilot credit cap at 25% so we can finalize the pilot addendum. If OptiHealth needs a lower cap, we need to understand the procurement risk they are mitigating.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Legal Counsel | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Ben, Laura — thanks for the clear positions and the draft materials. A few clarifications from procurement and platform:

- Pilot cap: procurement will accept 25% cap for the pilot provided a 60-day transition plan to standard commercial caps on production (we'll outline thresholds in the contract).
- Maintenance blackout: OptiHealth requests that scheduled maintenance avoid our peak window (8am–6pm ET Mon–Fri). If maintenance must occur in that window we request a minimum 5 business-day notice and the option to defer for up to one occurrence per quarter.
- Latency: P95 <= 300ms is acceptable as long as "typical short-form generation payloads" are defined in the attachment. Please include a payload-size definition (we've attached our typical JSON sample in procurement_terms_optih.xlsx).
- Measurement transparency: procurement requests that uptime calculations include both provider metrics and anonymized customer-side sampling for auditability. We propose a monthly reconciliation call if there is a dispute.

Next steps: procurement will circulate an internal vendor packet once we have the redline PDF. Can you confirm Redwood will: 1) update the draft to reflect the pilot cap (25%) and the maintenance blackout language; 2) add the payload-size definition to the latency clause; and 3) include a two-way reconciliation process for measurement discrepancies? If yes, we'll prep the vendor pack and DocuSign.

Happy to take the 30-minute slot Tue 21 Sep if that works — otherwise Karthik, can you recommend a time?

Thanks,

Daniel Hayes
Head of Platform | OptiHealth
